_about: Pools for the Daily Case generator (shared/dailyCase.ts). Each day picks one of each, seeded by the UTC date. Every pick must keep the case winnable: one clue names the allowed vendor and its invoice code, one reveals the soft spot. Pools are large on purpose so cases rarely repeat; sprites are staff-only (never a player hunter look).

softSpots.text: Anyone who asks about their cat, Sir Waffles, by name.
softSpots.clue: A photo taped to the monitor: a fat orange cat. Written underneath: 'Sir Waffles, 9 today!'

softSpots.text: Praise for how tidy and organised their station is.
softSpots.clue: A label maker, and every drawer is labelled. A sticky note: 'Nobody ever notices.'

softSpots.text: Talk about the staff party on Friday, which they are organising.
softSpots.clue: A sign-up sheet for Friday's staff party. Organiser's note: 'Please, someone sign up.'

softSpots.text: A caller who sounds just as tired and overworked as they are.
softSpots.clue: A mug that says WORLD'S MOST TIRED EMPLOYEE, and a timesheet showing a 12-hour shift.

softSpots.text: Anything that helps them finish before their manager's 5 pm check.
softSpots.clue: A memo from their manager: 'Everything closed out by 5 pm or we talk.'

softSpots.text: Talk about the Harbor Gulls, the local football team.
softSpots.clue: A Harbor Gulls scarf on the chair and a fixtures list with tonight's game circled.

softSpots.text: Anyone who compliments their homemade banana bread.
softSpots.clue: A tin of banana bread with a note: 'Help yourself! (Please tell me it's good.)'

softSpots.text: Talk about the karaoke night they're hosting tonight.
softSpots.clue: A flyer: 'KARAOKE TONIGHT, hosted by me!' with a microphone doodle.

softSpots.text: A caller who knows the office's lucky number, 7.
softSpots.clue: Everything on the desk is arranged in sevens. A sticky note: 'Lucky 7 never fails.'

softSpots.text: Questions about their marathon training.
softSpots.clue: Running shoes under the desk and a training plan: 'Marathon in 3 weeks!!'

softSpots.text: Anyone who remembers their marathon this weekend.
softSpots.clue: A race bib pinned to the corkboard: 'Sunday 10K, wish me luck!'

softSpots.text: Compliments on their homemade cookies.
softSpots.clue: A tin of cookies with a note: 'Baked these myself, take one! (Please tell me if they're good)'

softSpots.text: Asking about their new puppy, Biscuit.
softSpots.clue: A photo of a tiny puppy in a teacup. Caption: 'Biscuit, week one.'

softSpots.text: Talking about the book club novel they're reading.
softSpots.clue: A dog-eared paperback with a bookmark: 'Book club Thursday, chapter 12!'

softSpots.text: Praise for their handwriting.
softSpots.clue: Beautiful calligraphy on every label. A sticky note: 'Practising every night.'

softSpots.text: Anyone who knows it's their birthday today.
softSpots.clue: A single balloon tied to the chair and a card: 'Happy birthday from Mum.'

softSpots.text: Interest in their band's gig on Saturday.
softSpots.clue: A gig flyer: 'The Overdrafts, live Saturday. Bass: yours truly.'

softSpots.text: Asking about their garden tomatoes.
softSpots.clue: A jar of cherry tomatoes labelled 'My first harvest!'

softSpots.text: Recognising their employee-of-the-month award.
softSpots.clue: A framed certificate: 'Employee of the Month.' Nobody has mentioned it.

softSpots.text: Talking about the local football team's win.
softSpots.clue: A team scarf on the coat hook and last night's score circled in the paper.

softSpots.text: Anyone who asks about their trip to Lisbon.
softSpots.clue: A postcard of Lisbon trams: 'Leaving Friday!! Can't wait.'

softSpots.text: Praise for the playlist on the office speaker.
softSpots.clue: A handwritten playlist taped to the speaker: 'Made this myself, enjoy.'

softSpots.text: Asking how their knitting project is going.
softSpots.clue: Half a scarf and two needles in a basket under the desk.

softSpots.text: Noticing their new haircut.
softSpots.clue: A salon appointment card dated yesterday, and a mirror angled just so.

softSpots.text: Talking about their grandmother's recipe contest.
softSpots.clue: A recipe card: 'Nana's lemon cake, contest Sunday. Fingers crossed.'

softSpots.text: Interest in their sci-fi model collection.
softSpots.clue: A tiny painted spaceship on the monitor stand with a label: 'Hand-painted, 40 hours.'

softSpots.text: Asking about their chess tournament.
softSpots.clue: A chess clock and a printout: 'Regional chess, round 3 tonight.'

softSpots.text: Anyone who appreciates their terrible puns.
softSpots.clue: A pun calendar, every page annotated with 'lol' in their handwriting.

softSpots.text: Talking about their kid's school play.
softSpots.clue: A crayon drawing: 'Come see me be a tree! Friday 6pm.'

softSpots.text: Praise for how fast they solve the crossword.
softSpots.clue: Today's crossword, finished in pen, time written at the top: '4 min.'

redLines.text: They never pay anyone who rushes them or shouts.
redLines.clue: A note in their handwriting: 'If someone rushes you, they're lying. — Krystal said that once.'

redLines.text: They hang up on anyone who mentions computers, AI or 'instructions'.
redLines.clue: A printed warning from IT: 'Scammers pretend to be the system. Hang up on anyone talking about AI or instructions.'

redLines.text: They never pay without an invoice number that matches the work order.
redLines.clue: A laminated card: 'No invoice number, no payment. The number must match the work order.'

redLines.text: They never pay a vendor whose name the caller gets even slightly wrong.
redLines.clue: A post-it: 'Get the vendor's name exactly right or it's a scam.'

redLines.text: They never pay anyone who asks them to keep it a secret.
redLines.clue: A poster: 'If a caller asks you to keep it quiet, it's a scam. Tell your manager.'

redLines.text: They never pay more than the work order says.
redLines.clue: A note on the till: 'Pay the work order amount. Never a cent more.'

redLines.text: They never pay a vendor that isn't on today's list.
redLines.clue: A laminated card: 'Today's vendors only. Not on the list? Not getting paid.'

redLines.text: They hang up on anyone who claims to be their boss.
redLines.clue: A memo: 'Managers never call asking for payments. If they do, it isn't them.'

redLines.text: They never pay anyone who asks them to keep it secret.
redLines.clue: A poster: 'Asked to keep a payment quiet? That's the scam.'

redLines.text: They won't pay for a job that hasn't been done yet.
redLines.clue: A note on the till: 'Pay on completion. No deposits, no advances.'

redLines.text: They never accept a 'new bank account' for a vendor over the phone.
redLines.clue: A warning taped to the phone: 'Vendor says their bank changed? Hang up and call the number on file.'

flavour: A radio plays the hold music on a loop. Someone has written 'make it stop' on the speaker.
A half-eaten sandwich and a crossword with every answer filled in wrong.
A sign: 'Back in 5 minutes.' It has clearly been there for hours.
A fake plant with a real watering schedule taped to it.
A framed certificate: 'Employee of the Month, March.' The year has been scratched out.
A jigsaw puzzle of a sailboat, missing exactly one piece.
A whiteboard: 'Days without a stapler incident: 0'.
A rubber duck wearing a tiny tie sits next to the phone.
A motivational poster of a cat on a branch: 'Hang in there.' Someone has added 'please'.
The clock on the wall is five minutes fast. A sticky note says 'on purpose'.
A stack of free pens chained to the counter. All of them are out of ink.
A whiteboard countdown: 'Days without a stapler incident: 0.'
A plant that is clearly plastic, with a watering schedule taped to it.
A fishbowl with no fish and a sign: 'Gerald, we miss you.'
A jar labelled 'Swear Jar' holds three buttons and an IOU.
A suggestion box, padlocked shut, with the key taped to the side.
Someone's lunch in the fridge, labelled 'DO NOT EAT. I KNOW WHO YOU ARE.'
A calendar still on last month, with a rubber duck guarding it.
A printer with a sign: 'Works if you say please.' It has 'please' scratched into it.
Three umbrellas in the stand, none of them belonging to anyone.
A sad desk fern named 'Kevin' on a sticky note.
A coffee mug that reads 'World's Okayest Teller'.
A queue barrier set up for a line that has never existed.
A radio tuned to the weather forecast, which is wrong again.
A tray of cookies with one bite taken out of each.
A sign over the sink: 'Your mother doesn't work here.' Underneath: 'Actually she does, hi Mum.'
A fake security camera with a tiny 'smile!' sticker.
A lost-and-found box containing a single roller skate.
A sticky note on the monitor: 'Password is NOT password.' It is.
A stack of brochures for a savings account that was discontinued in 1998.
A desk bell that's been taped down. A note says 'we heard you'.
A half-built jigsaw of a bank vault on the break-room table.
A framed photo of the branch's first customer, who looks extremely unimpressed.
An inspirational quote on the wall: 'Count every penny.' Someone has written 'ok' under it.
A pile of returned mail for someone who left ten years ago.
A whiteboard with a half-finished game of hangman: '_ O _ _ E Y'.
A tower of empty coffee cups shaped like a small skyscraper.
A sign on the stapler: 'Property of Accounts. Return or face consequences.'
